AccessGrant.description: A short-lived access token for one device.

risk_ceiling.description: The highest risk this device may approve; `None`: no limit.

Approval.description:
A question the owner must answer before work goes on. Pending until
exactly one of: answered, expired (nobody answered in time: the call is
not run, and it is not a refusal) or withdrawn (its turn stopped, or the
daemon restarted).

card.description:
The card's typed facts, when the asker gave them. Left out in
compact frames.

channel.description:
The chat the card is also shown in (`telegram`...), if any besides
the app.

detail.description: The exact command or arguments. Left out in compact frames.

expires_at_ms.description: When it expires unanswered; `None` when the asker set no deadline.

options.description: The answers offered, in display order.

summary.description: One plain sentence: what will happen.

asked_by.description: The helper asking; `None` for the assistant itself.

oneOf.description: Allow it for the rest of this session.
Allow this kind of call from now on.
Allow a call (a command, a request, a tool use).
Confirm a scheduled goal.
Confirm an Autopilot posture.

Nobody answered in time. The call did not run; this is not a
refusal.

The question went away unanswered: its turn was stopped, the card
could not be shown, or the daemon restarted.

The work read content from outside and the clean check could not
confirm this step fits the request.
The owner said no to an earlier step of this run.

AttachmentRef.description: A file a client uploaded before sending its message.

Capability.description:
An optional feature, named instead of a version bump. A client lists the
ones it wants in `hello`; the server lists the ones it offers in
`welcome`, and only those it offers apply.

oneOf.description:
Short frames: an approval's summary without its detail or card, no
`turn_delta` or `turn_status`. The default for a watch.
Streaming `turn_delta` events.
`goal_updated` events.
Files with messages, through upload slots.
Push notifications through a relay.

The agent may move this connection's view (`view_action` events):
open a session, show an approval or a piece of work, focus a pane.
Sent only to the connection whose message started the turn, never
replayed, and never able to answer, pair, send or stop anything.
Run a command on the owner's computer.

looks_inside.description: Folders a read-only command only looks inside.

oneOf.description: Let the browser open a site on this computer.
Use a tool; `what` completes "wants to …".
Not run yet.

ClientFrame.description: A frame from a client to the daemon.

oneOf.description: The first frame on a socket.

resume_from.description:
The last `seq` the client applied; `None` for a client with no
cache. Within the retention window the gateway replays every
event after it, otherwise it sends a snapshot.

token.description:
The access token, for clients that cannot set an
`Authorization` header on a WebSocket (browsers).

oneOf.description:
A command. Answered by exactly one ack or error with the same
`request_id`; a retried id gets the original answer.

device.description: The device's name as the owner knows it ("Pixel 9").

ClientKind.description:
The kind of client, so the daemon can tailor what it sends and the owner
can see which device acted.

oneOf.description:
A smartwatch: short actions, compact frames, a risk ceiling on what
it may approve.
A script or other program.

Command.description: What a client asks the daemon to do.

oneOf.description: Start a session (no `session_id`) or continue one.

attachments.description: Files uploaded beforehand; needs the `attachments` capability.

mid_run.description:
What to do with it when the session is already working
(protocol 1.3). `None`: the agent reads it and decides.

oneOf.description: Stop everything the session has running (`/cancel all`).
Stop one entry of the running-work list.

before.description: Messages before this one (its id); `None` for the newest.

oneOf.description: Start the session afresh (`/clear`), keeping its history on record.
An existing slash command, until it has a typed command of its own.
Running tasks, pending approvals and the last reply, in one call.
The state a snapshot frame carries, on demand.

How the daemon itself is doing: version, models, usage, schedules,
background jobs, queues and health checks (protocol 1.2).

Messages of every session whose text holds all of `query`'s words,
newest first (protocol 1.3).

The slash commands the owner can run, for a client's completion
list (protocol 1.3).
What the daemon remembers about the owner (protocol 1.3).
Forget one remembered fact, by its `id` from `list_memories`.

`send_message`: the message was taken; what happens next arrives as
events of `session_id`.

`stop_turn` and `cancel_task`: what was stopped, in plain words, as
read back afterwards.
`resolve_approval`: this answer settled the approval.
`clear_session` and `run_slash`: the command's reply.
`search_messages`.
`list_commands`.
`list_memories`.
`forget_memory`: the fact is no longer recalled.

Enrollment.description:
Where a pairing stands (`GET /client/v1/enrollments/{offer_id}`, and
the owner's `GET /client/v1/pairing/offers/{offer_id}`).

oneOf.description: Not redeemed yet.
Redeemed; waiting for the owner.

ErrorCode.description: The closed set of error codes.

oneOf.description:
Authenticated, but not allowed: an approval above this device's risk
ceiling, a post into another chat's session.

The state moved on: an approval already resolved (the message names
the winning outcome).

Event.description: Something that happened. Durable unless noted.

oneOf.description: The owner (or someone in a shared chat) said something.

A message from the daemon outside a turn's reply: a queued-message
notice, an answer about running work, a background job's report.
Ephemeral: a chunk of the reply as it streams (capability `deltas`).
Ephemeral: what the turn is doing.

The turn waits for the owner to do something outside the chat
(finish an OAuth sign-in in a browser).

text.description: The final reply, as Markdown; empty when there was none.

resolved_by.description: Who answered; `None` when nobody did (expired, withdrawn).

oneOf.description: Only with capability `goals`.

Ephemeral, and only to the one connection that declared
`view_actions` and sent the turn's message: the agent asks this
client to move its view. The client shows a short note of what moved
and why. A view action only changes what is on screen; it never
answers an approval, pairs or revokes a device, sends a message or
stops work.

reason.description: Why, in a few plain words, for the note the client shows.

EventsPage.description:
`GET /client/v1/events` answers with this: the event frames after
`since` (or a snapshot frame first, when `since` is out of the retention
window), and the `since` to ask with next.

GoalRunInfo.description: One run of a background goal, judged by what it left behind.

outcome.description: What the run reported; `None` when it reported nothing.

session_id.description: The session the goal reports into, to open.

HistoryMessage.description: One message of a session's transcript.

tools.description: For a reply: the tools its turn used, in order (protocol 1.3).

source.description: Where it came from, in a word or two.

MidRun.description: Where a message sent while its session works goes.

oneOf.description: Into the work running now: the agent takes it into account.
After the work running now, as a turn of its own.

fell_back.description: Calls answered by a fallback model.

OfferRequest.description:
The owner's offer to pair a device (owner only:
`POST /client/v1/pairing/offers`).

confirm_in_session.description:
The chat where the owner confirms the device; `None` to confirm
with `POST /client/v1/pairing/offers/{id}/decision`.

OwnerInfo.description: The daemon's owner, as the gateway knows them.

PairingDecision.description: The owner's answer to a pending pairing made without a chat.

code.description: What the owner types on the device ("K7Q2-9FZD").

fingerprint.description: Identifies this daemon; the device checks the redeem reply matches.

link.description:
The same as a link, for a QR code:
`aidaemon-pair:?gateway=<url>&offer=<id>&code=<code>&fp=<fingerprint>`.

public_url.description:
Where devices reach the gateway now (a live tunnel origin, the
configured address, or loopback). Absent from older daemons.

Pane.description: A part of a client's screen.

retryable.description: Whether the same request may succeed later.

ProtocolVersion.description: A protocol version. Same major: compatible.

device_name.description: The device as the owner will see it ("Pixel 9").

public_key.description: The device's P-256 public key, SEC1 uncompressed, base64url.

scopes.description: The scopes asked for; empty: all of them.

channel.description: `app` for a client of this protocol, else the chat (`telegram`...).

Risk.description: How much is at stake, from the daemon's typed rating. Ordered.

schedule.description: The schedule as the owner wrote it ("every weekday at 9").

Scope.description: What a device's token may do.

oneOf.description: Read sessions, history, events, tasks and approvals.
Send messages, stop and cancel work, run commands.
Answer approvals (within the device's risk ceiling).

SearchHit.description: A message that matched a search.

snippet.description: The text around the first match, plain.

ServerFrame.description: A frame from the daemon to a client.

oneOf.description: The answer to `hello`.

latest_seq.description: The newest `seq` in the log when the socket opened.

oneOf.description:
Everything a client needs when it cannot resume: drop the cache and
start from this state. Events after `seq` follow.

seq.description: Per owner, gap-free; `None` for an ephemeral event.

request_id.description: `None` for an error that answers no command (a bad frame).

signature.description: The signature as `r || s` (64 bytes), base64url.

writable.description:
Whether clients may post into it. Sessions of other chats are
read-mostly in v1: watch, stop and answer approvals there, but post
from that chat.

SlashCommand.description: A slash command, as a completion list shows it.

Snapshot.description: What a client needs when it cannot resume.

SystemStatus.description: How the daemon itself is doing, for the app's System area.

checks.description: The owner's health checks of their own services.

jobs.description: The daemon's own background jobs (memory upkeep, pruning, ...).

model.description: The model normal requests use, and the ones tried when it fails.

model_calls.description: Model calls over the last 24 hours; `None` when not recorded.

runs.description:
Background goal runs of the last 24 hours, newest first (protocol
1.3).

usage.description: Tokens per day and model, newest day first (the last 7 days).

TaskSummary.description:
One entry of a session's running-work list: a turn, a helper (sub-agent)
or a background command.

id.description: Stable across the daemon's life; `cancel_task` takes it.

number.description: The short number `/cancel <n>` takes in the chat.

oneOf.description: The reply was delivered.
The agent had nothing to say.
The work goes on in the background; its report comes later.

TurnStatus.description: What a running turn is doing.

oneOf.description: A rendered checklist of the turn's plan, as Markdown.
Anything else worth a line ("helper started: …").

ViewAction.description:
Where the agent asks a client to take its view. Every variant only
changes what is on screen: none carries a decision, a message or a
device, so none can answer an approval or act for the owner. Kinds a
client does not know read as `Unknown` and are ignored.

oneOf.description: Open a session's transcript.
Bring a waiting approval's card into view (not answer it).
Show an entry of the running-work list.
Move the keyboard to a pane.
Clear the composer's target, so the next message starts a session.
Show the paired devices.
